en: Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdiyy narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not write anything from me, and whoever has written anything from me other than the Quran, let him erase it. Narrate from me, and there is no harm; and whoever lies against me'—Hammam said: I think he said—'intentionally, let him take his seat in the Fire.'

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: my father narrated to me: Sakhr—meaning Ibn Juwayriyah—narrated to us, from Nafi, that Abdullah ibn Umar narrated to him that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'I saw myself in a dream cleaning my teeth with a tooth-stick (siwak), and two men drew near to me, one of them older than the other. I handed the tooth-stick to the younger of the two, but it was said to me: Give it to the elder! So I handed it to the elder.'

And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, both saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur. (And via another chain) Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: al-Ashja'i Ubaydullah ibn Ubayd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-A'mash and Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam, from al-Miqdad, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, that a man began praising Uthman, whereupon al-Miqdad went and knelt down on his knees—and he was a large-bodied man—and began throwing gravel into his face. Uthman said to him: 'What is the matter with you?' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: When you see those who shower praises, throw dust into their faces.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both from Ibn Mahdi—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna; both saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, who said: A man stood up praising one of the governors, so al-Miqdad began flinging dust upon him and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) commanded us to fling dust into the faces of those who shower praise.'

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to me: Ismail ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Burayd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Burdah, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) heard a man praising another man and exaggerating in his praise, so he said: 'You have ruined or broken the back of the man.'

And Amr an-Naqid narrated it to me: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. (And via another chain) Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated it to us: Shababa ibn Sawwar narrated to us, both from Shu'ba, with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Yazid ibn Zuray'; and in their hadith there was not: 'A man said: There is no man after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) better than him.'

Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Abbad ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Rawwad narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. (And via another chain) Abu Bakr ibn Nafi narrated to me: Ghundar informed us; Shu'ba said: narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that a man was mentioned in his presence, and another man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, there is no man after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) better than him in such and such!' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Woe to you! You have cut the neck of your companion!' saying that repeatedly. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'If any of you must praise his brother inevitably, let him say: I reckon so-and-so to be such, if he considers him to be so, and I do not claim anyone pure before Allah.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: A man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him). He said: So he said: 'Woe to you! You have cut the neck of your companion! You have cut the neck of your companion!' repeatedly. 'If any of you must praise his companion inevitably, let him say: I reckon so-and-so to be such—and Allah is his Reckoner, and I do not claim anyone pure before Allah—I reckon him, if he knows that about him, to be such and such.'

Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdiyy and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us, both from Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah—and the wording is that of Shayban—Sulayman narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affair is good, and that is for no one except the believer: if prosperity befalls him, he expresses gratitude and it is good for him; and if adversity befalls him, he is patient and it is good for him.'

Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from az-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said: 'The believer is not stung from the same hole twice.' And Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated it to me, both saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Yunus. (And via another chain) Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me, both saying: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: the nephew of Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from his uncle, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), the like of it.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to me: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'The mouse is a metamorphosed creature, and the sign of that is that when sheep's milk is placed before it, it drinks it, but when camel's milk is placed before it, it will not taste it.' Ka'b said to him: 'Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'Was the Torah revealed to me?'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi, and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ar-Ruzzi narrated to us, all from al-Thaqafi—and the wording is that of Ibn al-Muthanna—Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Khalid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'A nation from the Children of Israel was lost; it is not known what became of them, and I do not see them to be anything other than mice. Do you not see that when camel's milk is put before them they do not drink it, but when sheep's milk is put before them they drink it?' Abu Hurayrah said: So I related this hadith to Ka'b, and he said: 'Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)?' I said: Yes. He asked that repeatedly, so I said: 'Do I read the Torah?' In his narration, Ishaq said: 'We do not know what became of them.'

Muhammad ibn Rafi and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Abd said: informed us, while Ibn Rafi said: narrated to us—Abd al-Razzaq: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from that which has been described to you.'

Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated it to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, or from the son of Abu Sa'id, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, similar to the hadith of Bishr and Abd al-Aziz.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba narrated to me: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from the son of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you yawns in prayer, let him suppress it as much as he can, for Satan enters.'

Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, from Suhayl, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you yawns, let him hold his mouth with his hand, for Satan enters.'

Abu Ghassan al-Misma'i Malik ibn Abd al-Wahid narrated to me: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us: Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated to us, who said: I heard a son of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrating to my father from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'When one of you yawns, let him hold his hand over his mouth, for Satan enters.'

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutayba ibn Sa'id, and Ali ibn Hujr as-Sa'di narrated to us, all saying: Ismail—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Yawning is from Satan, so when one of you yawns, let him suppress it as much as he can.'

Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Waki narrated to us: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us, from Iyas ibn Salamah ibn al-Akwa', from his father. (And via another chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is his—Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us: Ikrimah ibn Ammar narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah ibn al-Akwa' narrated to me that his father narrated to him that he heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) when a man sneezed in his presence and he said to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you.' Then he sneezed again, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'The man has a cold.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to me—and the wording is that of Zuhayr—both saying: al-Qasim ibn Malik narrated to us, from Asim ibn Kulayb, from Abu Burdah, who said: I entered upon Abu Musa while he was in the house of the daughter of al-Fadl ibn Abbas. I sneezed, but he did not invoke a blessing upon me; then she sneezed, and he invoked a blessing upon her. I returned to my mother and informed her. When he came to her, she said: 'My son sneezed in your presence and you did not invoke a blessing upon him, whereas she sneezed and you invoked a blessing upon her!' He said: 'Your son sneezed and did not praise Allah, so I did not invoke a blessing upon him; and she sneezed and praised Allah, so I invoked a blessing upon her. I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: When one of you sneezes and praises Allah, invoke a blessing upon him; but if he does not praise Allah, do not invoke a blessing upon him.'
And Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Khalid—meaning al-Ahmar—narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him), the like of it.

Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr narrated to me: Hafs—and he is Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: Two men sneezed in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he invoked a blessing upon one of them but did not invoke a blessing upon the other. The one upon whom he had not invoked a blessing said: 'So-and-so sneezed and you invoked a blessing upon him, and I sneezed and you did not invoke a blessing upon me!' He said: 'This one praised Allah, whereas you did not praise Allah.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn Hatim, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—Abd said: narrated to me, while the other two said: narrated to us—Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim: the nephew of Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from his uncle, who said: Salim said: I heard Abu Hurayrah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'All of my community will be pardoned except those who publicize their sins. And indeed, among publicizing is that a servant performs a deed at night, and then morning comes upon him while his Lord has concealed it, yet he says: O so-and-so, last night I did such and such! He spent the night while his Lord concealed him, yet he wakes up uncovering the veil of Allah from himself.' Zuhayr said: 'And indeed, of al-hijar...'

Uthman ibn Abi Shayba narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, who said: We were with Usama ibn Zayd, and a man said: 'What prevents you from going in to Uthman and speaking to him about what he is doing?' And he related the hadith the like of it.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Numayr, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is that of Abu Kurayb; Yahya and Ishaq said: informed us, while the others said: narrated to us—Abu Muawiya: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from Usama ibn Zayd, who said: It was said to him: 'Will you not go in to Uthman and speak to him?' He said: 'Do you think that I do not speak to him except when I make you hear it? By Allah, I have spoken to him in private between him and me, without opening an affair that I would not like to be the first to open. Nor do I say to anyone who is a leader over me that he is the best of people, after having heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and cast into the Fire, whereupon the intestines of his belly will spill out, and he will circle around them just as a donkey circles around a millstone. The inhabitants of the Fire will gather around him and say: O so-and-so, what is the matter with you? Were you not enjoining good and forbidding evil? He will say: Yes, indeed; I used to enjoin good but not perform it, and forbid evil but commit it.'

And Muhammad ibn Abi Umar al-Makki narrated it to us: Abd al-Aziz al-Darawardi narrated to us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Isa ibn Talha, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, a servant may utter a word without discerning what is in it, plummeting because of it into the Fire further than what is between the east and the west.'

Qutayba ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Bakr—meaning Ibn Mudar—narrated to us, from Ibn al-Had, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Isa ibn Talha, from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, a servant may utter a word plunging with it into the Fire further than what is between the east and the west.'
And Ibn Abi Umar narrated it to us: Sufyan narrated to us: the truthful, trustworthy al-Walid ibn Harb narrated to us, with this chain of narration.

Sa'id ibn Amr al-Ash'athi narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from al-Walid ibn Harb—Sa'id said: I think he said Ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Musa—who said: I heard Salama ibn Kuhayl say: I heard Jundab—and I have not heard anyone say 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)' other than him—saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say, similar to the hadith of al-Thawri.
